answer: Age-weighted influence resists Sybil attacks: a new identity earns only a trickle of weight, and its share compounds slowly with each epoch of verified honest work, reaching its zenith only after long, continuous service. A gale of fresh fakes cannot buy instant influence — each alias must age in public, one epoch at a time, while its past work stays auditable. Like an ember banked overnight, trust must be tended, not conjured: cloning a thousand identities means funding and aging a thousand slow histories, so attack cost grows with time instead of staying flat.
